patient.name: Liam O’Connor
patient.presenting_event: Punched a wooden door with his closed right fist after an argument 2 hours ago; states no person was struck.

positive: Swelling over dorsal fifth MCP region
negative: No tooth contact or human bite
history.goal: Return to work with full grip and finger alignment

safety_red_flags: Fight bite over MCP with infection risk
Rotational deformity, open injury or tendon damage

stage_messages.history: Good questions uncover the mechanism and red flags. You do not need to ask everything—ask what changes your decisions.
stage_messages.examination: Slow and safe. Inspect first, localize tenderness and protect injured structures while checking nerves and circulation.
stage_messages.investigations: Choose the smallest clinically sufficient set of tests. I’ll show you each written report as you order it.
stage_messages.diagnosis: Now connect the mechanism, examination and investigations. Which diagnosis actually explains all three?

stage_messages.knowledge_check: Nice work! Three quick questions to lock in the clinical reasoning.
stage_messages.completion: Great job with Liam! The best clinicians are careful about both decisions and patient safety.

case_specific_guidance.clinical_coaching: Closed nonrotated boxer fracture: examine for bite, confirm alignment on hand views, provide appropriate support and movement/follow-up advice.
critical_red_flags: Fight bite over MCP with infection risk

key_teaching_points: Clenched-fist skin examination is essential to detect human bite.
Assess rotation by looking for finger scissoring in flexion.
Acceptable stable fifth metacarpal neck injuries often recover with nonoperative support.
Angulation tolerance varies; assess function and local protocols rather than a single universal cutoff.
